Forensic Design Verification: 5 System Flaws & Operational Exceptions

Analysis of PLC Functional Specification NCX-MEA-01-2516-CS-SP-0001.16.APU vs live roadside operations

1. Asymmetric Ramp Logic (S6 vs S2) Root Flaw

Under Technical Query TQ158 (Spec p. 235), designers added Rule 2k for exit ramp S6 to pre-emptively START a fan if flow drops below -10 m³/s. However, Section S2 on-ramp was given no pre-emptive start rule—only a rule preventing fan stops, which does nothing when fan count is zero.

2. Hair-Trigger 0-Second Alarm Delay Debounce Flaw

Functional Spec pages 228 & 265 set Section S2 Portal Emission Alarm Delay = 0 Seconds. The instant rolling flow dips below 0 m³/s for even 1 second due to wind gusts or truck turbulence, a SCADA Level 2 alarm triggers and sends email notifications.

3. Single-Input Zone Decoupling Controller Flaw

Zone 3 Controller (ctrJFTVZ203) uses process values strictly from downstream mid-tunnel sensors (S4/S5). Mainline freight satisfies the mid-tunnel target, leaving the on-ramp aerodynamically starved with zero jet fans running.

4. Exit Portal Emissions (S8 & N8) Bypass Flaw

Exit portals (S8 and N8) experienced 599 alarms when positive airflow discharged past the portal instead of being evacuated by ventilation station stacks, demonstrating issues beyond on-ramp S2.

5. Graphic Anomaly (13 vs 17 Fans) SCADA Flaw

Operational engineers observed Northbound running 17 fans while the overview graphic showed 13 fans. This discrepancy occurs because local controller groups across N1-N7 stage fans independently, some of which are not mapped to the main graphic group.

Recommended Engineering Actions Action Plan

1. Add S2 Pre-emptive Fan Start: If S2 flow ≤ 0 m³/s, start 1 S2 jet fan.
2. Set Alarm Delay to 120s: Filter out momentary turbulent eddies.
3. Nighttime SP Adjustment: Bump overnight setpoint to 210 m³/s to maintain positive draft.
